svg.title: The virtio status handshake
svg.desc: The driver writes Status 0 (reset), then 0x1 ACKNOWLEDGE, 0x3 adding DRIVER, accepts features (VERSION_1, bit 32), writes 0xb adding FEATURES_OK and reads it back, sets up queue 0 (size 16, three ring addresses, QueueReady 1), then writes 0xf adding DRIVER_OK. Bits only accumulate; writing 0 is the one way back. The device refuses FEATURES_OK if the driver accepted a bit it never offered or did not accept VERSION_1, ignores queue writes while a queue is ready (except a QueueReady 0 before DRIVER_OK, which unfreezes it) or once DRIVER_OK is set, and answers a ring outside RAM at DRIVER_OK with DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET (64) and a configuration interrupt.

g.text: The probe's handshake, as traced on a real Mac
The device has the last word
FEATURES_OK with an unoffered bit, or without VERSION_1: not latched
a skipped step or a cleared bit: ignored (bits only accumulate)
queue writes while the queue is ready, or after DRIVER_OK: ignored
(before DRIVER_OK, writing QueueReady 0 still unfreezes the queue)
a ring outside RAM at DRIVER_OK: DEVICE_NEEDS_RESET (64) + config interrupt
narrow or misaligned control access: read as zero, write ignored
Writing 0 to Status resets the device: the one way back.
